definition_zh: n. 瑕疵；污点；伤疤；v. 损毁；玷污
definition_en: a small flaw that spoils the perfection of something, or to spoil it
scene: 买家对着灯细看白玉，指出一点黑痕。The scandal blemished his spotless reputation.
sceneCN: 这里 blemish 是动词「玷污」（第 2 个义项：损坏原本完美之物）；句意是丑闻玷污了他无可挑剔的名声。

derivatives.zh: un- 加 blemished，义为「无瑕的；清白的」

senses.title: A small physical flaw
senses.definition: a mark or spot that spoils the surface or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 损坏表面或外观的痕迹或斑点
senses.example: The apple had one small blemish on its skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这只苹果表皮上有一处小瑕疵。
senses.why: Old French blessier meant to wound; a blemish is a tiny wound on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 blessier 意为「伤害」，blemish 即表面上的小伤。

senses.title: To spoil perfection
senses.definition: to damage the good condition or reputation of something
senses.definitionCN: 损坏某物完好的状态或名声
senses.example: The scandal blemished his spotless reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻玷污了他无可挑剔的名声。
senses.why: What wounds a surface wounds, too, a name held to be flawless.
senses.whyCN: 能伤表面者亦能伤被视为无瑕之名。

senses.title: A moral stain
senses.definition: a fault that stains an otherwise clean character or record
senses.definitionCN: 玷污本来清白品格或记录的过错
senses.example: One late payment was the only blemish on her credit file.
senses.exampleCN: 一次迟付款是她信用档案上唯一的污点。
senses.why: Records and characters are surfaces the eye of society inspects.
senses.whyCN: 记录与品格是社会目光检视的表面。

senses.title: A skin imperfection
senses.definition: a spot, pimple, or mark on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上的斑点、丘疹或痕迹
senses.example: The cream promises to clear skin blemishes.
senses.exampleCN: 这款面霜号称能清除皮肤瑕疵。
senses.why: Skin is the most inspected surface of all, so beauty talk uses the word most.
senses.whyCN: 皮肤是被检视最多的表面，美妆语境因此最常用此词。

senses.title: A flaw in goods offered for sale
senses.definition: an imperfection that lowers the value of merchandise
senses.example: Blemished goods were sold at a discount.
senses.exampleCN: 有瑕疵的商品打折出售。
senses.why: Perfect surfaces fetch full price; any wound shows in the tag.
senses.whyCN: 完好表面值全价，一处伤痕便体现在价签上。

senses.title: A defect in a polished argument or text
senses.definition: a small weakness in something otherwise excellent
senses.definitionCN: 整体出色之作中的小弱点
senses.example: The only blemish in the essay is a weak conclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章唯一的疵点是结尾无力。
senses.why: Writing is judged as a surface too; one dent catches the eye.
senses.whyCN: 文章亦被当作平面来审视，一处凹陷格外扎眼。

senses.title: A ritual imperfection in offerings
senses.definition: a defect that makes an animal unfit for sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 使牲畜不合祭祀之用的缺陷
senses.example: The law forbade sacrificing animals with any blemish.
senses.exampleCN: 律法禁止献祭有任何瑕疵的牲畜。
senses.why: The altar demands perfection; the oldest moral use grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 祭坛要求完美，最古老的道德用法由此生长。

senses.title: To mar beauty of sound or movement
senses.definition: to spoil the flawless quality of a performance
senses.example: One missed note blemished an otherwise perfect recital.
senses.exampleCN: 一个错音破坏了本已完美的独奏会。
senses.why: A performance is a surface of time; one dent is heard by everyone.
senses.whyCN: 表演是时间织成的表面，一处凹陷人人听得见。

intro.en: Blemish comes from Old French blemir, to wound or bruise.
intro.cn: blemish 来自古法语 blemir「伤害；使瘀青」。

items.en: probably from Frankish blesni, a wound, a Germanic borrowing into French.
items.cn: 一般认为出自法兰克语 blesni「伤口」，属日耳曼语借入法语。

items.en: blemissier and blemir meant to injure, bruise.
items.cn: 古法语 blemissier 与 blemir 意为「伤害、打伤」。

items.en: the legal sense of a defect in title or character formed in law French.
items.cn: 法律法语中形成了「产权或品格缺陷」的专业义。

items.en: English took blemish for both physical marks and moral stains.
items.cn: 英语于 13 至 14 世纪借入，兼指身体痕迹与道德污点。

items.en: now common in cosmetics, quality control, and moral commentary.
items.cn: 今常见于美妆、品控与道德评述。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the blem- sound; the near-meaning group gathers flaw words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 blem- 音；近义组收瑕疵类词。

an imperfection lacking a part or quality

normalIntro.en: Blemish grew from a word for wounding; now it marks any small flaw.
normalIntro.cn: blemish 源自「伤害」之词，今指一切小瑕疵。

normal.cn: unblemished 是无瑕的反义形容词。

normal.en: It works for skin, goods, and reputations.
normal.cn: 它可用于皮肤、商品与名声。

normal.en: A blemish is small; a ruin is total.
normal.cn: blemish 指小瑕疵，毁坏则是全盘的。

normal.en: Legal English still says title without blemish.
normal.cn: 法律英语仍说 title without blemish。

normal.en: Both noun and verb uses are common.
normal.cn: 名词与动词用法都常见。

abstract.en: See one black dot on a bowl of white pearls.
abstract.cn: 看一碗白珍珠上的一粒黑点。

abstract.en: Feel a fingernail scratch across polished glass.
abstract.cn: 感受指甲划过抛光玻璃的刺感。

abstract.en: Picture a perfect legal record spoiled by one late form.
abstract.cn: 想象被一份迟交表格毁掉的完美档案。

examples.en: The scandal blemished his spotless reputation.
examples.cn: 丑闻玷污了他无可挑剔的名声。

examples.en: The apple had one small blemish on its skin.
examples.cn: 这只苹果表皮上有一处小瑕疵。

examples.en: One late payment was the only blemish on her credit file.
examples.cn: 一次迟付款是她信用档案上唯一的污点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不乐意是」——玉上有个黑点，买家不乐意是必然的。

root: 古法语 blemir「伤害；使瘀青」（一般认为出自法兰克语 blesni「伤口」，日耳曼借词），经盎格鲁-法语在法律语境中形成「缺陷」义，13 至 14 世纪进入英语，兼指身体瑕疵与道德污点。

sensesIntro.en: From a wound on skin to a stain on character, blemish names the small flaw that perfect things cannot hide.
sensesIntro.cn: 从皮肤之伤到品格之污，blemish 指完美之物无法掩盖的小瑕疵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one black dot on flawless white jade
core.cn: 核心意象：无瑕白玉上的一粒黑点

branches.en: Marks on physical surfaces and skin
branches.cn: 实体表面与皮肤上的痕迹

intro.en: The blemish family is small but common in quality talk.
intro.cn: blemish 词族不大，但常见于品控语境。

latinIntro.en: Germanic source via Old French; no Latin core.
latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼词源经古法语传入，无拉丁核心。

items.example: a stain on the family name
